newsitem.title: USA: S. Dakota soy harvest progresses, corn still wet.
newsitem.headline: S. Dakota soy harvest progresses, corn still wet.

text.p: Soybean cutting made good progress in the week ended Sunday but much of the corn was too wet to harvest, South Dakota's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
"Most of the corn was still too wet to harvest but the warm, dry weather allowed some progress and helped the corn dry down," the report said.

Soybean harvest was 46 percent complete, well above last week's level of 13 percent but trailing the average of 51 percent. Corn was seven percent harvested, compared with six percent last week and 26 percent for the five-year average.
Corn was rated two percent poor, 19 percent fair, 52 percent good and 27 percent excellent. Soybeans were rated three percent poor, 19 percent fair, 55 percent good and 23 percent excellent.
Winter wheat was 93 percent seeded, behind the average of 97 percent. Several areas reported some intended acreage will not get planted due to the lateness.
Soil moisture rated seven percent short, 91 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
